Session

You might say

After signing in, why does the page stay signed in after refresh?

State a service keeps for a signed-in person and can look up using a browser-held identifier·After sign-in, a request that matches the cookie domain, path, and browser policies can carry a session identifier, which the service uses to find a still-valid session. A session may expire or be revoked, prompting another sign-in; this differs from the current password check failing.
Know first
Authentication
Session
From sign-in to expiry: how a session recognizes the same person
Browser · Sign-in / Network

Welcome back

Account lin@example.com　Password ••••••••

Signed in · server stores session_7

Response header Set-Cookie: session_id=session_7; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure

After verification, the service creates or updates a session and uses Set-Cookie to store an identifier in the browser. The cookie usually does not contain the full session record.

What a session goes through

The server creates a session at sign-in: After credentials pass, the server creates a session state for this person and gives the browser an identifier.

Matching requests carry the identifier: Requests carry it when cookie domain, path, and browser policies match; the service looks up the session to keep the user signed in.

It fails after expiry or clearing: When the session expires or the identifier is cleared, the server no longer recognizes it and the page asks for sign-in.

What people often confuse

Being asked to sign in again does not mean the password is wrong: session expiry is the signed-in state ending, while authentication failure is the identity not being accepted. Separate state is gone from identity is wrong first.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

Users are asked to sign in again every half hour. Check the session lifetime setting and state its current value; if it is too short, adjust it to a reasonable duration and confirm an hour of continuous use stays signed in.
